Subject: Next steps after demo — hosting preference?

Thanks for the demo today — good walk-through, appreciated. A quick recap / clarification from my side so we can align internally before the technical follow-up: 

- Our current serving stack is a self-hosted Triton pipeline running on a small in-house GPU cluster (NVIDIA A40s). It's been okay for low volume but we want predictable latency & fewer ops headaches.
- Expected steady-state: ~100-150 inference requests / sec for text generation across a couple routes; peak bursts up to ~300 RPS. Target P95 latency < 150ms for short prompts.
- Data: most traffic is de-identified, but we DO process PHI in some routes. So data residency + VPC/network isolation are important.
- Budget: procurement prefers to keep monthly spend under a hard cap; open to reserved capacity if it makes sense for predictability.

Questions:
1) From a migration perspective, what’s your recommended path given our current Triton setup: Hosted API (fastest), Dedicated pool (predictable), or Private VPC/on-prem?
2) How frictioned is moving model artifacts (custom weights & tokenizer) from our S3 to your platform?
3) Any initial lift-and-shift gotchas we should flag to infra (KV cache behavior, prefix caching, tokenization differences)?

I attached an architecture diagram and a short latency CSV from last week's load test. Would like a short written recap we can share with procurement and infra.

—Samir
Senior Engineering Manager, Avery Health

Samir — thanks for the clear summary and for the attachments. Below is a concise qualification and recommended next steps you can share with the Avery procurement/infra teams.

Short answer / recommendation:
- If PHI and full network isolation are must-haves day one, Private VPC (customer-managed VPC peering or private deployment) will be the target. If you need a quicker path to validate prompts and cost, we often pilot on Hosted API (short-term) then transition to Dedicated or Private once SLAs and throughput are validated.

Tradeoffs at a glance (high level):
- Hosted API: fastest to spin up, easiest for prompt tuning and evals; lowest ops on your side but limited network isolation unless using secure tunnels. Good for short pilots.
- Dedicated: Reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and single-tenant performance; supports strict SLAs and encryption-in-transit + at-rest. More control over instance sizing.
- Private VPC/On-prem: Full network control and compliance; longer procurement and setup (weeks). Best for PHI/regulatory requirements.

Migration notes specific to Triton -> Redwood: 
- Model artifacts: We can pull from S3 with an IAM role we provide, or you can push via secure upload. Custom weights & tokenizers are supported, but we do an integrity & behavior check during onboarding.
- KV/prefix caching: Our cache semantics differ slightly; expect smaller warm-up latencies on first traffic. We'll recommend a cache-warm strategy during cutover.
- Tokenization: Small differences can affect token counts; we'll run golden prompt tests and report token delta which helps cost projections.

Immediate next steps (proposed):
1) Technical call (30 min) next Tues 10/13 to validate infra access, S3 paths, and pilot scope (load test window). 
2) Share a single procurement contact and any required compliance docs — we’ll send a tailored Private VPC checklist if PHI is in scope.
3) I’ve attached a concise comparison PDF (redwood-hosting-comparison.pdf) and a short pilot checklist we can turn into an action plan.

If that sounds good I’ll book the call and loop in our deployment engineer.

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Senior Solutions Lead — Redwood Inference

Hey Samir / Markus — a few technical clarifications from infra/ops perspective so the pilot can be scoped tightly: 

- Migration approach options:
  * Pilot on Hosted API: quickest for prompt & evaluation checks; helps quantify token economics and correctness against your golden prompts. Low friction but not ideal for PHI long-term.
  * Dedicated reservation (recommended mid-term): We reserve GPUs with node sizing similar to your current A40s; predictable throughput, better tail latency control.
  * Private VPC: we deploy a control plane with private connectivity. This requires network approval, cert exchange, and an initial runbook for failover — typically a multi-week setup.

- Model packaging: Send us the model artifact tar + tokenizer or give us an S3 role. We run a compatibility test (we'll report any ops-level incompatibilities, e.g., custom ops compiled against old CUDA).

- KV cache & warmup: For your burst profile we recommend a short, scripted warmup during cutover (5–10 minutes of representative traffic) and a conservative autoscale headroom of ~25% above expected peak initially.

- Metrics & testing: We’ll provide a small harness for golden-prompt comparison, plus a load test runner. We should agree on 3–4 golden prompts that match PHI/anonymized real queries.

Could you confirm: (a) S3 bucket name & whether we can request a read role, (b) whether procurement requires SOC2 + HIPAA paperwork up front, (c) a point of contact for networking (VPC peering/firewall).

Thanks — I’ll prepare a short runbook draft after we get those answers.

—Karthik
Principal Infra Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
